subtype: Approach: seeking advice from a founder who failed [Action]
passage: Avni almost did not send the message. Irawati's startup had shut down last year, and asking about it felt rude. But on Saturday they sat in a small café in Pune, and Avni asked, "Which of your early costs do you wish you hadn't spent?" Irawati laughed, then counted on her fingers. "A fancy office lease. A full-time hire before we had customers. An expensive launch event. Legal templates I never used." Avni wrote them into her phone. "The things that felt like being a real company were the wasted ones." On Sunday night Avni redrew the first budget: no lease, freelancers instead of hires, no event. The total was smaller by almost a third, and she felt oddly relieved.

qa.q: Which costs did Irawati name as wasted?
qa.a: A fancy office lease, a full-time hire before customers, an expensive launch event, and legal templates never used.

qa.q: Why did Avni almost not send the message?
qa.a: Avni felt that asking about the shut-down startup would be rude, so was uneasy and hesitant.

qa.q: What could Avni do next after redrawing the budget?
qa.a: Avni could ask one more founder the same question, and check the new budget against real customers early.

qa.q: How might Irawati have felt being asked?
qa.a: Irawati may have felt willing to help, and maybe pleased that the failed startup's lessons were useful.

grounding: Avni asks a founder whose startup shut down which early costs were wasted, and the list changes how the first budget is drawn.

"Thanks for meeting me, Imran. I know it's awkward to talk about."
"It's fine, Vandana. The company's been closed a year. Ask."
"Specifically: what did you spend on early that you'd take back?"
He counted on his fingers. "The office in month two. Eighteen-month lease, and we were three people. A branding agency before we had a single customer. And the conference in Goa where we paid for a stall and got four leads."
"What would you have spent on instead?"
"Talking to customers. Petrol to visit them. A cheap prototype."
Vandana was writing fast. "And salaries?"
"We paid ourselves too soon. Should have waited until someone paid us."
She looked at her draft budget. Office: crossed out. Agency: crossed out. Conference: crossed out. "You just saved me about half my money."
"Then buy the coffee."

qa.q: What three early costs would Imran take back?
qa.a: The office lease in month two, a branding agency before any customer, and the conference stall in Goa.

qa.q: How did Vandana feel while crossing out three lines of the budget?
qa.a: Vandana felt relieved and grateful, realising the advice had saved about half the money.

qa.q: What else could Vandana ask other founders?
qa.a: She could ask what they wish they had spent more on, such as customer visits, to shape the new budget.

qa.q: What is it like for Imran to share his mistakes?
qa.a: It might once have been uncomfortable, but a year on Imran speaks plainly and seems glad the lessons can help someone else.

grounding: It shows a young founder meeting someone whose startup closed, asking exactly which early costs were wasted, and redrawing the first budget from the answers.

I'd heard Jahnavi's pet-food startup had shut down, and for weeks I felt too awkward to message her. Finally I asked if I could buy her a coffee and ask one question: which early costs were a waste?
She didn't hesitate. "Packaging. We spent a fortune on printed boxes in three sizes before we knew which one sold. And a full-time accountant in month one, for about twelve orders a week." She added, "Also the photoshoot. Customers bought because of reviews, not our photos."
That night I redid the budget for my candle business. Plain boxes with a sticker until I know my best seller. A part-time bookkeeper, once a month. No photoshoot; I'll use my phone and ask the first twenty buyers for reviews. The money saved went into samples for shops.
I sent Jahnavi a photo of the new sheet. She replied, "Wish someone had asked me this three years ago."
— Salma

Why did Salma feel awkward about messaging Jahnavi?

qa.a: Salma could wait a few months to see which candles sell best before ordering any printed boxes.

qa.a: Jahnavi may feel a little wistful, but glad the lessons can help someone avoid the same waste 🙂
